name: Trailer Fetcher
description: Finds and downloads missing local trailers for movies and TV series from YouTube via yt-dlp.
overview: Finds and downloads missing local trailers for movies and TV series from YouTube via yt-dlp.

versions.changelog: A run that gets YouTube-rate-limited can now wait and retry once instead of always stopping immediately. There's no reliable way to know when the limit actually lifts - YouTube's own message only states an upper bound ("...for up to an hour") - so this is a single bounded retry, not a backoff loop: on the first rate limit, the run waits a configurable delay (new "Rate-limit retry delay" setting, default 65 minutes - a bit past YouTube's own stated ceiling) and then resumes the same run from wherever it stopped (not a full restart), controlled by a new "Retry once if rate-limited" toggle (on by default). If the retry also gets rate-limited, the run stops for good rather than waiting and retrying again - continuing to hammer an apparently-still-active limit doesn't help and risks making it worse.

Two small polish items from live testing. (1) The rate-limit ERROR log line is now a fixed, short message ("...rate-limited by YouTube for up to an hour. Stopping the run now.") with a link to yt-dlp's own wiki page on the condition, instead of extracting/reformatting yt-dlp's raw stderr text. (2) The settings page's last-run-summary table had a generic "Metric / Value" header for movies but correctly showed "TV series" as a section label further down - movies now get their own "Movies" section label the same way, and the generic header row (which added nothing the section labels don't already say) was dropped.

Trimmed the rate-limit ERROR log line. 0.8.15.0's log included yt-dlp's entire raw warning paragraph verbatim - a lead-in sentence, the actual rate-limit notice, then yt-dlp's own "-t sleep" suggestion and a wiki URL, most of which is noise once our own message already explains what's happening and why. Now logs just the one sentence that matters ("The current session has been rate-limited by YouTube for up to an hour.") plus a short reason for stopping early. No behavior change, log output only.

Handle YouTube's own rate limiting instead of grinding through it. Confirmed live on a long run: once YouTube rate-limits a session ("The current session has been rate-limited by YouTube for up to an hour"), no client/format fallback helps, and continuing on to retry other clients or move to the next movie/series just wastes time against a block that won't lift itself any sooner - possibly making it worse. YtDlpClient now detects this specific condition and throws a distinct YouTubeRateLimitedException that propagates straight past every retry tier and out of the movie/series loop, stopping the whole run early - with whatever was found before it hit still logged/persisted the same way a cancelled run's partial summary already is (RunSummary's Aborted flag is now a StopReason string so the summary/log can say "YouTube rate-limited this session" specifically, not just "cancelled"). Also added a "Delay between requests" setting (default 3s, configurable, 0 disables it) - a plain per-invocation delay before every yt-dlp call, sized for this plugin's actual pattern of many short-lived separate invocations rather than yt-dlp's own "-t sleep" preset (which sleeps up to 20s per download, tuned for one long-running session working through a playlist).

Added a "Verbose logging" setting. Each rejected search candidate's specific reason ("Title mismatch: ...", "Duration > 300s: ...") is now only logged when it's turned on (off by default) - a movie/series that needs several fallback search stages before finding (or giving up on) a trailer can generate dozens of these lines, burying the handful that actually matter for a normal run. Each search stage's overall outcome (what was searched, found or not) is still always logged regardless; this only trims the per-candidate detail within a stage, which matters most when actively diagnosing why a specific movie/series isn't finding a trailer it should.

Two fixes. (1) 0.8.12.0 over-corrected: forcing player_client=web for EVERY download whenever a cookies file was merely configured (regardless of whether that specific video needed it) reintroduced 0.8.10.0's "Only images are available for download" failure for ordinary, non-restricted videos, confirmed live. DownloadAsync now has three tiers instead of two: try the default client first, retry with player_client=web only if that failed AND cookies are configured (a targeted shot at the age-verification case), then fall back to mweb if that still fails too. (2) Fixed a year-range ("(1994-2019)", an anthology/box-set's airing span) not being recognized as a unit by the year-extraction regex - only the first year was getting stripped, leaving "( -2019)" behind in the resolved title. Confirmed live on a Shinichiro Watanabe anthology folder. Fixed in the shared TitleMatching.CleanMediaTitle since a movie box set could hit the same pattern.

Fixed a regression from 0.8.10.0 that broke cookies-based authenticated/age-restricted access: an age-restricted video failed with "Sign in to confirm your age" despite a valid, verified-account cookies.txt being uploaded. 0.8.10.0 removed the player_client override entirely, but it had been doing two different jobs - restricting to a now-stale "web,android,ios" list (correctly removed) and forcing player_client=web whenever cookies were configured (needed, and removed by mistake): a cookies file only actually takes effect on the "web" client, since the app-style clients (android, ios, mweb, tv, android_vr, ...) authenticate via device tokens and silently ignore a cookies file regardless of --cookies being set. CommonArgs now forces player_client=web again specifically when a cookies file is configured. Also updated DownloadAsync's mweb retry fallback to skip itself (retrying the same web-forced command instead) whenever cookies are set, since mweb doesn't honor cookies either and would have sent yt-dlp two conflicting player_client overrides in the same command.

Small polish from live testing. The candidate-rejection log line was ambiguous ("Title mismatch or missing keyword") when the code actually knows which one it was - split into two distinct, specific messages ("Title mismatch: ..." vs "Title matches, but no trailer keyword (trailer/teaser/...): ..."). Also dropped a manually-added inner quote pair around the candidate title in that message, which stacked with the logging backend's own automatic quoting the same way earlier quoting bugs did.

Found and fixed the actual root cause of the "Only images are available" failures (deno confirmed fully functional in 0.8.9.0's diagnostics). Removed the hardcoded --extractor-args youtube:player_client=web,android,ios override - it made sense when the standalone script was written, but confirmed live and by hand: it's become actively harmful as YouTube's defenses evolved (android/ios are now routinely filtered by SABR/PO-token requirements), while yt-dlp's own default client selection (actively maintained upstream to route around exactly this) found proper adaptive formats via a different client. That default choice isn't fully reliable either though - confirmed live and reproduced consistently by hand: its first-choice client's formats can extract fine but 403 on the actual download. DownloadAsync now tries the default first, and retries with an explicit player_client=mweb on failure specifically (not just repeating the same command) - mweb's own adaptive formats get filtered the same way, but it then falls back cleanly to a legacy, reliably-downloadable format instead of failing outright, confirmed consistent across repeated attempts. Verified the whole two-tier sequence end to end against the exact failing video before shipping.

Diagnostic-only addition. The previous release's added logging revealed the real yt-dlp error: "WARNING: Only images are available for download" - meaning YouTube served no real video/audio formats at all on that server, only storyboard images, which happens when YouTube enforces SABR-only streaming and the signature challenge solver can't actually run - even when a JS runtime binary is present on disk, since that doesn't prove it actually executes successfully from inside Jellyfin's own process (permissions/sandboxing can differ from a manual test). DependencyProvisioner now runs "deno --version" in that same execution context - once after downloading it, and once on every run where it was already present - and logs the result, to get a definitive per-run answer instead of inferring deno's health from a downstream symptom that has more than one possible cause.

Three fixes from live testing. (1) The "Last run" summary is now cancellation-safe: cancelling a run used to skip saving the summary entirely, leaving a stale summary from a previous run on display - the movie/series loops are now wrapped so the summary is always logged/persisted with whatever was found before it stopped (marked "cancelled - partial results"), then the cancellation is rethrown so Jellyfin's TaskManager still correctly reports it as cancelled rather than completed. (2) The summary now only shows a Movies or TV Series section for libraries actually in scope for that run, instead of always showing "Total Movies in Library: 0" for a run scoped to series-only libraries. (3) Replaced the full ISO "Completed" table row with a compact date + time + duration line above the table. Also added diagnostic logging (yt-dlp's WARNING lines, and the resolved yt-dlp/deno paths) to help pin down a reported case where every download failed with "Requested format is not available" on one server.

Two fixes. The settings page's "Last run" table styling never actually applied (confirmed against 0.8.6.0, incognito included): Jellyfin's dashboard loads a plugin's config page by injecting its body content into the existing app shell, which drops the page's own <head> - a <style> block there silently never took effect. Rewrote the table to style itself entirely via inline styles set in JS instead, which can't be dropped that way. Also added a single retry to YtDlpClient.DownloadAsync: a download that failed with "Requested format is not available" during a real run was verified (by hand, twice, with the exact same command) to succeed immediately after - a transient hiccup, not a persistent problem with that video - so one retry is cheap insurance against exactly that without masking a genuinely unavailable video, which will just fail again on the retry too.

Fixed a high-impact porting regression in TitleMatching.TitleMatches: the YouTube result title was never lowercased before the phrase-match regex ran against it, while the candidate side always was - and .NET's Regex.Match is case-sensitive by default, so "blue lock" (candidate) silently never matched "Blue Lock" (a title-cased YouTube title) even though they're the same title. The standalone script avoids this by lowercasing yt_title once at the top of its filter function; the C# port dropped that step. This was very likely the dominant cause behind most search-based "Title mismatch" rejections seen throughout testing (movies and series both, not just the two TV cases that surfaced it) - confirmed against the exact failing case ("Blue Lock - Official Trailer..." now correctly matches "Blue Lock"). Also fixed SeriesTitleCleanup leaving an empty "( )" behind when the season-range fragment it removes was fully inside a parenthetical ("Blue Lock (Season 1)" -> "Blue Lock ( )" -> now "Blue Lock").

Fixed wrong search queries for TV series bundled as a multi-season folder (e.g. "... S1 - S5 [Full Series] ..."): a season-range fragment ("S1", "S1 - S5", "Season 1-5") was surviving into the resolved title, since nothing in the shared title-cleanup logic knows about season ranges (a movie title never has one) - confirmed live on "Food Wars! (Shokugeki no Soma)", whose search queries all carried a spurious "S1" because Jellyfin's own matched Name already had it before the plugin ever saw it. Added Services/SeriesTitleCleanup.cs, a small series-only post-processing step (deliberately not folded into the shared ItemMetadata/TitleMatching, since this noise is TV-specific) that strips a season-range fragment from the resolved title/variants before they're used for search or the trailer filename. Verified against the exact failing case plus several variants (Season 1-4, S01-S04) and confirmed it leaves unrelated content alone (e.g. a hypothetical title like "S1mone").

The settings page's "Last run" summary is now a real styled HTML table (header row, right-aligned values, a distinct section divider for TV series counts) instead of an unstyled table with no visual structure.

Fixed a title-matching bug that broke every search for "5 Centimeters per Second" (and would break any title genuinely starting with a number - "12 Monkeys", "300", "8 Mile", etc.): the scene-release-cleanup heuristic stripped any leading "number + whitespace" as if it were a track/episode number, with no structural signal distinguishing that from a title that just starts with a digit. Removed that overly broad rule - kept the punctuation-anchored one ("01. ", "01 - ", "01_", still needed for real scene-numbered filenames) since a genuine title essentially never has a period/dash/underscore directly after a leading number. Verified against both the exact failing title and a set of real scene-numbered filenames to confirm the legitimate case still works. This heuristic was ported verbatim from the standalone script, which likely has the same latent bug.

Fixed a real miss reported from live testing: probing a candidate (yt-dlp -j --skip-download) hard-failed with "Requested format is not available" for some videos, discarding otherwise-fully-extracted title/duration/webpage_url metadata over a format-selection problem that doesn't matter during a metadata-only probe. Added --ignore-no-formats-error to the probe call specifically (not the actual download, which does need a real format) - verified against the exact failing video from the report: probing now returns full metadata, and the subsequent download succeeds too (yt-dlp falls back to a pre-merged format when the preferred bestvideo+bestaudio combo isn't available, e.g. due to a missing PO token). Not series-specific despite surfacing during series testing - RemoteTrailers URLs are sourced identically for movies and series, this was always a latent gap in the movie path too.

Refactor - per feedback, verified the movie/series duplication from 0.8.0.0 and found the SeriesMetadata.cs/SeriesTrailerSources.cs title/year-resolution and source-query-building logic was byte-for-byte identical to MovieMetadata.cs/TrailerSources.cs aside from variable names and comments (both are plain BaseItem lookups with nothing movie- or series-specific in them), so there was no actual behavior to isolate by keeping them separate - only a maintenance burden of every future fix needing to be applied twice. Merged them into one shared Services/ItemMetadata.cs and widened TrailerSources.Build to take a BaseItem. ProcessMovieAsync/ProcessSeriesAsync in FetchTrailersTask.cs stay separate, since what they actually do genuinely differs (rename/migrate + file-specific validity checking for movies vs. a plain folder-exists check for series). No functional change.

Added TV series support - series-level trailers only (Services/SeriesMetadata.cs, Services/SeriesTrailerSources.cs), sharing the same library selection as movies but otherwise deliberately kept as a fully separate code path from the movie logic rather than a shared generic one, so a change intended for one media type can't silently affect the other. Checked Jellyfin's actual entity model first: Series has its own LocalTrailers/RemoteTrailers (same shape as Movie), but Season has no equivalent property at all - despite Jellyfin's docs showing a trailers/ folder example nested under a season folder - so season-level trailers aren't implemented until that's verified against a real library. No rename/migrate step for series: a series always already lives in its own dedicated folder. The settings page's "Last run" summary and the main log's TRAILER SYNC SUMMARY both show series counts alongside the movie ones now.

Logged paths (directory entries, rename/migration targets) now show relative to the movie's own library root (via BaseItem.GetTopParent()) instead of the full container path, so log lines aren't dominated by a repeated mount-point prefix. Also fixed one path that was still logged in full (unlike its sibling lines) in the rename-folder failure case. No behavior change - display only.

First real-run fixes from live testing. Fixed a class of log-quoting bugs where a value already wrapped in manual quotes in the message template got double-quoted (the logging backend quotes string values by default). Also dropped the library's GUID from the scan-start log line (not useful in the UI) and fixed a related bug where a DRY-RUN prefix fragment spliced in through its own placeholder got quoted on its own. Tightened the yt-dlp/deno download timeout from 5 minutes to 2 and gave it a clear, actionable message on failure (mentioning GitHub's release CDN specifically) instead of leaving a run looking hung - a download that times out no longer masks a deliberate task cancellation as an ordinary download failure, either. The last run's summary is now also persisted and shown on the settings page, not just buried in the log.

Removed the "yt-dlp executable" setting entirely - the plugin now always uses its own self-managed yt-dlp/deno (see 0.6.0.0), never a system installation. Letting that path vary would mean supporting whatever yt-dlp version/flag combination a user happens to have installed, instead of the one this plugin is actually built and tested against - and this plugin's whole point is working out of the box on a stock Jellyfin install with no server-side setup or path fiddling.

yt-dlp and the deno JavaScript runtime it needs no longer have to be installed on the server - the plugin now downloads and manages both itself (Services/DependencyProvisioner.cs), verifying checksums and self-updating yt-dlp every 24h, so it works on a stock jellyfin/jellyfin container with no customization. The 'yt-dlp executable' setting is now empty by default (auto-managed) instead of defaulting to "yt-dlp"; set it to a specific command/path to opt back out and use your own installation instead. Evaluated and rejected two alternatives (documented in the README): the Ytdlp.NET fluent wrapper package (still needs the same underlying binary, and its metadata API is single-URL only - doesn't support this plugin's multi-candidate probe-then-filter strategy) and MeTube (a second container/service with no metadata-only probe API and a separate cookie config).

Ported the standalone script's actual trailer fetching: title/year resolution, multi-stage YouTube search query building, duration+title/keyword candidate filtering, original-file renaming, and folder migration all now run for real (FetchTrailersTask was previously a wiring stub that only counted movies). Runs entirely in-process against ILibraryManager - no NAS path mapping, no HTTP calls to Jellyfin's own API, no browser cookie jar (uses the uploaded cookies.txt), library scans triggered via ILibraryManager.QueueLibraryScan() directly. Shells out to a yt-dlp executable (new 'yt-dlp executable' setting, default "yt-dlp" on PATH) for the actual YouTube search/download, since there's no C# equivalent - REQUIRES yt-dlp (and a JS runtime, deno or node) to be installed wherever the Jellyfin server process itself runs; ffmpeg is reused from Jellyfin's own configured encoder, no separate install needed. See the README's new Requirements section.

Fixed the scheduled task showing up in its own untranslated "Library" group instead of joining the real Library group on non-English servers. The task's Category was the literal string "Library", but built-in library tasks (e.g. RefreshMediaLibraryTask) get their Category from ILocalizationManager.GetLocalizedString("TasksLibraryCategory") - the same server-side-localized key that this task now uses too, so both group under the same (correctly translated) label.

Fixed the "0 movies found" library-scoping bug, confirmed via diagnostic logging (1026 movies found server-wide, 0 when scoped to a library known to contain real movies). The fix was hand-building TopParentIds from VirtualFolderInfo.ItemId directly, which does not reliably match what TopParentIds-based filtering expects. Now resolves each configured library via ILibraryManager.GetItemById() and queries via InternalItemsQuery.Parent instead.
